id: rank-two-spin-trapping-depth-three-blind-proof
kind: route
title: Commutators kill primitives in KU, complexification has kernel eta·KO, and eta^3 = 0
target: rank-two-spin-trapping-blind-to-depth-three-brackets
requires: [trapped-spin-bordism-class-over-any-spin-seed-factor]
---

Write G = U(2). As a space G ≅ S^1 x S^3, so Sigma^∞ of every G^n and every
smash G^{∧n} is a wedge of spheres. KO^* of such a space is a free
KO_*-module, and external products give KO~^*(G∧G) ≅ KO~^*(G) (x)_{KO_*} KO~^*(G).

**Step 1: KU^*(G) is generated by primitives.** Let a = det^* of the
generator of K^{-1}(S^1), and b = sigma^* iota, where sigma: G -> U is the
standard representation and iota in K^{-1}(U) = [U, U] is the identity. The
group law of K^{-1}(X) = [X, U] is pointwise multiplication, so
mu^* iota = pr_1^* iota + pr_2^* iota. Since det and sigma are homomorphisms,
a and b are primitive. b restricts to a generator of pi_3 U on SU(2), so
KU~^*(G) is spanned over KU_* by a, b and ab.

**Step 2: the commutator kills KU~^*(G).** Let c: G x G -> G be
c(g, h) = g h g^{-1} h^{-1}. For primitive p, the inverse map sends p to −p, so
c^* p = p(x)1 + 1(x)p − p(x)1 − 1(x)p = 0. The map c^* is a ring homomorphism,
so it kills the reduced ring generated by a and b.

**Step 3: one eta per bracket.** Take z in KO~^*(G). Then c^* z restricts to
zero on G ∨ G, because c(g, 1) = c(1, h) = 1. So c^* z lies in the split summand
KO~^*(G∧G). Its complexification is c^* of the complexification of z, which
is 0 by Step 2. Wood's cofibre sequence Sigma KO -eta-> KO -> KU gives
exactness of KO^{*+1}(Y) -eta-> KO^*(Y) -> KU^*(Y) for every Y, here the
reduced theory of G∧G. So c^* z = eta·w with
w = sum_i y_i (x) z_i and y_i, z_i in KO~^*(G).

**Step 4: induction.** Put c_1 = id and c_{j+1} = c o (1 x c_j): G^{j+1} -> G, so
c_{j+1}(g_j, ..., g_1, h) = [g_j, c_j(g_{j-1}, ..., g_1, h)]. Claim: c_j^* z is
in eta^{j-1}·KO^*(G^j) for all z in KO~^*(G). For j = 1 there is nothing to
prove. Given the claim for j,

    c_{j+1}^* z = (1 x c_j)^*(eta·sum_i y_i (x) z_i) = eta·sum_i y_i (x) c_j^* z_i,

which lies in eta^j·KO^*(G^{j+1}). A depth-j bracket of maps M -> G is
f_j = c_{j+1} o (g_j, ..., g_1, h), so f_j^* z is in eta^j·KO^*(M). Apply this
to z = x = rho^* u, which is reduced. Since f_j takes values in SU(2), where
rho is the identity, f_j^* x = f_j^* u. With eta^3 = 0 in KO_*, f^* u = 0 for
j = 3. This is (a).

**Step 5: characteristic numbers of the fibre.** Let y be a regular value of
f: M -> S^3 = SU(2) and F = f^{-1}(y), with normal framing f^*(T_y S^3) and
the induced spin structure. Then TF (+) R^3 = TM|_F, so every Stiefel–Whitney
class and KO-Pontryagin class of F is the restriction of the corresponding
class of M. The KO-pushforward along i: F -> M satisfies i_!(1) = f^* u,
because u is the KO-Thom class of the framed point. By the projection
formula, for every KO-characteristic class pi^J,

    <pi^J(F), [F]_KO> = <pi^J(M)·f^* u, [M]_KO> = 0.

The same argument in mod-2 cohomology gives
<w_I(F), [F]> = <w_I(M)·f^* u_2, [M]> with u_2 in H^3(SU(2); Z/2).
H^*(G; Z/2) = Λ(x_1, x_3) with x_1 = det^* and x_3 primitive (degree 3 has no
room for cross terms). So Step 2 applies verbatim, and f_j^* u_2 = 0 for
j >= 1. This is (b).

**Step 6.** By Anderson–Brown–Peterson (recalled, theorem number not
re-verified), a spin manifold with vanishing Stiefel–Whitney and
KO-characteristic numbers bounds. So [F] = 0. By Toms (6) and Part 1,
Remark 2.2 of `class-three-spin-bordism-trapping-2026-09-12.md`, the
isomorphism Omega~^Spin_m(S^3) ≅ Omega^Spin_{m-3} takes [M, f]_red to [F]. The
seed-factor formula nu^M((f o pr_M) (+) 1_Q) = <c_r(Q)^2, [X]>·[M, f]_red
(trapped-spin-bordism-class-over-any-spin-seed-factor) then gives (c). □

*Sanity check.* On T^2 x S^3 with f = [alpha o s_2, [alpha o s_1, omega o z]],
Step 4 gives f^* u in eta^2·KO^*, and the class-three lane finds exactly
eta^2 on the top cell: the Arf-invariant-one torus.
